68: In the Trading panel, controls whether the "Sell Outfits" button will allow selling outfits even when there is no outfitter at which to buy them back.
69: In the Trading panel, controls whether or not to confirm sales of all outfits in cargo.
70: In the Trading panel, controls whether or not to confirm sales of minables, specials and other flotsam that may have been picked up.
71: Whether fast-forward should be in sync with the state of CapsLock on the system. The default setting keeps them in sync if the fast-forward key is CapsLock.
72: Apply a cinematic zoom in and out when you are landing and taking off.
73: The speed of scrolling in panels that can scroll.
74: For how long you need to hover over an item to show its tooltip.
75: The format that dates in the game are displayed in.
76: Toggle whether parentheses are shown around potential profits and losses in the ports map mode.
77: Control an indicator that occurs when you enter a system with a planet you must land on for a mission.
79: - "message": displays a message with the planets you must land on.
80: - "both": displays the message and plays a notification sound.
81: Include message logs in pilot files so they are not lost when closing the game or reloading the save file. This will increase save file sizes and may increase load times. The stored log history can be cleared from the message log panel.
82: Whether your monitor should be able to dim and turn off or change to the screen saver while the game is open.
83: Controls the ammo refill behavior when you enter the outfitter.
84: - "always": ammo will be automatically refilled if you have the credits for it.
85: - "when free": ammo will be automatically refilled only if it doesn't cost you anything, such as when you have spare ammo in cargo or storage.
86: - "ask": you will be prompted to refill any missing ammunition upon entering the outfitter.
87: - "never": you will always have to manually refill your ammunition.
88: Choose the theme of the title bar, or leave "system default" to use system settings. (Available on Windows 10 or newer; on Windows 10, the game window must be resized or restarted in order for the change to take effect.)
89: Control the appearance of window corners. (Available on Windows 11.)
90: Whether a confirmation dialog will be displayed when you attempt to demand tribute from a planet.
91: - "off": you will never be asked for confirmation.
92: - "friendly only": you will only be asked for confirmation against planets that you are friendly toward.
93: - "always": you will always be asked for confirmation.
94: The lowest value that an outfit or ship can depreciate to relative to its full price. All plundered, captured, or gifted items start at this value, and all purchased items start at 100% value and then depreciate toward this value according to the other depreciation gamerules.
95: The number of days that must pass before a newly purchased outfit or ship will begin to depreciate. This allows you to have a short amount of time to test out an item and then sell it back at full value if you decide that you do not like it.
96: The number of days that must pass, after the grace period has ended, in order for an outfit or ship to become fully depreciated.
97: The percentage of an item's depreciable value that it maintains day over day. Only impacts the exponential term of the depreciation calculation. If set to 100%, an item will still linearly lose value.
98: The number of frames on average that the game waits before attempting to spawn a person ship. The game rolls a random number between 0 and this value minus one every frame. (There are 60 frames in a second.) If the value lands on 0, a person ship spawn attempt is made. In other words, higher values result in lower spawn rates of person ships.
99: When a person ship spawn attempt is made, this is the "weight" of the chance of having the spawn attempt fail. Each person ship has a "weight" associated with it which determines its chance of spawning. The chance of any single person ship spawning is its weight divided by the sum of the weights of all person ships and this value. That means that the chance of a spawn attempt failing is this number over that same sum.
100: Randomly spawned NPCs with the "mining" personality will spend this many frames mining in the current system before deciding to do something else. The purpose of this limit is so that NPC ships can be seen by the player to show how to mine without stripping the system bare of minable asteroids. This limit does not apply to mining ships that are spawned by a mission.
